title: Nehogy...!: A Gentle Warning with the Imperative

sections.title: Softer than a prohibition, sharper than a suggestion
sections.content: *nehogy* (built from *ne* + *hogy*) opens a warning about something the listener should make sure NOT to do. The verb after it takes the same form as a direct command (the imperative you already know), but *nehogy* itself changes the tone from a flat prohibition into a worried, caring warning — closer to "watch out that you don't..." than to "don't!"

sections.title: Plain prohibition vs. worried warning
rows: Whatever you do, don't forget! (a worried warning)

items.english: Make sure you don't forget to lock the door!
Be careful not to hurt his/her feelings when you tell him/her!
Make sure you're not late for the meeting!

sections.content: *nehogy* always takes the imperative, never the plain present tense — *Nehogy elfelejted* is a common learner mistake; the correct form is the imperative *elfelejtsd*, exactly as if *nehogy* weren't there at all.
